name: Theology of Rap

global_influences.evidence: Secondary sources describe T.O.R. as run on a strictly commercial model, distinguishing them from more scene/community-oriented crews, but do not document specific named artist influences.
global_influences.source: Bangladeshi hip hop scene retrospectives (see sources)

local_adaptation_notes: Not documented in detail in available sources beyond the group rapping in Bangla; no specific analysis of lyrical localisation located yet.
sound_evolution_summary: Best known for the album Hip-Hop Jati (14 April 2010, Deadline Music, produced by GT Production), including the track "Mudrar E'pith Opith." Also active as event organisers, hosting concerts that gave a platform to upcoming rappers — a notable contribution to scene infrastructure beyond their own recordings.
concert_culture_notes: Credited in secondary sources with hosting concerts/events for upcoming rappers, making them one of the earlier organisers (not just performers) in the Bangladeshi hip-hop scene.
listener_community_notes: Named alongside Deshi MCs and Uptown Lokolz (`uptown-lokolz`) as one of the pioneering 2000s crews establishing Bangladeshi hip-hop. Member Grand T is separately credited (Wikipedia: Bangladeshi hip hop) as the first Bangladeshi rapper to pursue international collaboration (2009), linking this crew to the genre's early internationalisation.

sources.title: THE HIP-HOP STORY — The Daily Star
